summary: Crafty's moment-to-moment combat layer now meets a 2026 bar. It has a world hitstop, a readable 380 ms windup, a perfect dodge that staggers, a held heavy attack and four Aspects with real verbs. The layer that should give those verbs something to answer is far behind, and one number undercuts most of it: the player walks at 14 m/s in every direction, while the fastest chaser manages 6 m/s and the dodge ends slower than walking. So every melee fight is optional, and walking backwards while clicking beats every telegraph. Encounters arrive one random mob at a time, 70% hostile by day, with no packs, camps, elites or scaling by distance. The night 'siege' adds 4 to a spawn cap. Quests are counters, dungeons are empty rooms, and shrines do not do what their lore promises. The climax ignores the combat verbs: the dragon's bite and roar give no warning (the roar has no range check at all), the perfect dodge and the heavy cannot affect it, and it reads as a purple box. Reading the code, the signature Wildheart transform and the heavy attack also cannot be performed on iPad. The best moves are cheap and mostly self-contained modules. In order: (1) a combat walk speed separate from travel speed; (2) the dragon put on the same windup and perfect-dodge rules as the mobs; (3) a 90-second opening that gives a new player the transform in the first minute; (4) a hold fix on touch; (5) a spawn director that gives day, night and the frontier distinct shapes.

findings.title: Combat is optional: the player walks 2-5x faster than anything that chases them
findings.observation: BASE_MOVE_SPEED is 14 m/s and applies the same in every direction, backpedalling included. It was raised from 10 for travel to the far Blight Heart. Chase speeds once a mob is aggro'd: husk 3.0 m/s, emberhusk 3.45, skeleton 3.75, duskhound 4.8, brute shoulder charge 5.4, skitterling 5.7, spider 6.0. The dragon's phases move at 4-7 m/s. The dodge bursts from 28 to 10 m/s, so it ends slower than walking. Player melee reaches 4.5 m against the default mob reach of 2.5 m. So the 380 ms windup, the perfect dodge, the brute's brace-charge-winded cycle and the hound's flank only matter to a player who chooses to stand still. Only skeleton arrows and the dragon's range-free roar reliably reach a player who walks away.

findings.proposal: Add a small self-contained module, game/combatStance.js, with inCombat(now, {nearestAggroDist, lastHitAt, lastDealtAt}). It returns true while an aggro'd hostile is within 18 m, or for 2.5 s after the player deals or takes damage. moveSpeed reads it: 6.5 m/s in combat (backpedal x0.8), and the 14 m/s travel stride out of combat. The stride ramps in over 0.6 s with a +4 degree FOV kick and a faster footstep tempo, so the shift is felt; travel to the lair stays as Kevin asked. The dodge then becomes the real escape (28 to 10 m/s, faster than the combat walk). Trim the melee cone range from 4.5 to 3.2 m so spacing matters. Raise the hound and skitterling chase multipliers so they press at about 6 m/s. Gates: a unit test on the stance. An e2e test with a real held S key against an aggro'd husk asserts the gap closes within 3 s; it is red on today's code. The control: with no aggro, the player covers at least 12 m/s. A mutation forcing 14 m/s in combat must turn the e2e red. The feel constants go to Kevin as FYI.

findings.title: The climax ignores the combat verbs: unreadable boss attacks, no perfect-dodge or heavy interaction, and a box silhouette
findings.observation: The dragon's bite deals damage whenever the player is within 5 m, on a 2 s cooldown, with no windup. The Phase 2 roar fires every 4.2 s with no distance check and no tell: 32 damage plus a 36-unit knockback wherever the player stands, with a 'Pushed back!' toast after the fact. The perfect dodge only searches ECS mobs; the boss is a separate entity, and the heavy's stagger excludes bosses. So the game's two newest skill verbs do nothing in its one boss fight. Phase 1 orbits 13 m up, beyond the melee cone's 2.2 m vertical cutoff, so 40% of its HP is spells only. Each 2.4 s fireball posts a toast, so text stands in for a telegraph. Return tiers only scale numbers. boss-closeup.png shows a purple box with a cube head and two stick wings, not a dragon. The entrance is silent (STATUS 'no ROAR'), although a 'roar' synth voice already exists for Wildheart.

findings.proposal: Put the dragon on the mob rules. Give it a windupUntil and run the bite and roar through attackPhase. Add a bossAsTarget() adapter to perfectDodgeTargets: a perfect dodge of the dive-bite staggers the dragon for 1.4 s, its wings fold and it lands. That stagger becomes Phase 1's melee opening and gives every phase a skill answer. The roar gets a 900 ms inhale tell (hinged jaw opens, throat emissive ramps, playSpatialSound('roar') pitched down), a 9 m radius with falloff, and is dodgeable through i-frames. Three heavies inside one stagger knock it down for 3 s (the riposte multiplier applies). Replace the per-attack toasts with ground decals; the lava ring telegraph already shows the pattern. Each return tier adds one move: tier 1 a dive-bomb with a ground-shadow telegraph, tier 2 a tail sweep. Rebuild the silhouette from about 30 boxes (5-segment neck and 6-segment tail with lagged follow, 3-bone membrane wings, hinged jaw), merged into 1-3 draw calls. Gates: an e2e perfect dodge on a planted bite windup (the same method as perfect-dodge.spec). A roar control: hit at 5 m, missed at 11 m. A capture A/B of boss-closeup.

findings.title: The first minute promises a block sandbox and hides the signature for 10-20 minutes
findings.observation: The title tagline reads 'Build, Craft, Cast Spells, Explore' and promises neither the four Aspects nor the dragon. On spawn the player gets two one-time text toasts, an 8 s controls sheet, and three counter quests: First Blood 0/1, Hunter 0/5, Builder 'place 20 blocks' 0/20. The game's signature moment is the Wildheart third-person transform reveal. Reaching it takes two talent points (level 3, 250 XP), a full 100-point Ferocity bank (about 7 hostile day kills at 16 each) and a 0.45 s held R. Nothing tells a new player it exists before then.

findings.proposal: Build a 60-90 s 'Ember Prologue' from parts that already exist, run once per profile under the same localStorage-once guard. At spawn the siege horn sounds. A scripted wave (2 husks and 1 brute, spawned by type 20 m out on the compass-marked bearing) comes at the Hearth gate. Old Pike's line teaches dodge (Shift). When the brute's windup starts, the game grants one free roar: canEnter is bypassed once and a flag is saved. The 1.2 s reveal plays, the player clears the wave as the fire comet, and the form ends with 'The ember sleeps. Earn it back: reach level 3, open Talents (U).' The first tracked quest becomes 'Earn the Roar', not 'Place 20 blocks'. Rewrite the title tagline around the actual promise (Aspects, frontier, dragon). Gates: an e2e on a fresh profile reaches title, first kill and beastFormActive within 120 s; a returning profile skips it. A mutation that removes the one-time bypass must turn it red.

findings.title: On iPad the Wildheart transform and the heavy attack cannot be performed (from reading the code)
findings.observation: The touch Aspect ring pulses a verb's intent for TAP_HOLD_MS = 120 ms on pointer-up. The roar state machine cancels its charge on the frame the roar intent drops, and the charge needs ANTICIPATION_SEC = 0.45 s, so a touch roar always cancels. The heavy is wired only to mouse button 0 and the T key. The touch action button fires performVerb on pointer-up, so no hold is possible. iPad is a hard target (pillar P4), and these are the signature Aspect and the newest combat verb. I derived this from the code and have not driven it on a device.

findings.proposal: Make the roar sector press-and-hold: pointerdown sets the intent true; pointerup, pointerleave or pointercancel sets it false. Draw a radial fill showing the 0.45 s charge. Give the action button the same treatment: pointerdown calls pressHeavy('touch') and pointerup calls releaseHeavy. The tap still throws the light swing at once, which heavyAttack's design already supports. Gates: a Playwright touch-emulation e2e (or touch-probe) with a full Ferocity bank. Holding the roar sector 600 ms gives beastFormActive; a 120 ms tap does not (the control). Holding the action button 800 ms on a husk deals at least 1.8x the tap's damage. Drive it once on a real iPad before claiming it fixed.

findings.title: No encounter design: a one-at-a-time random trickle, 70% hostile by day, with no packs, camps, elites or scaling by distance
findings.observation: spawnMob picks one type per call by flat weight across all 10 types and places it at a random point 28-85 m away. By day 70% of picks are hostile (6.15 of 8.75 weight), so with a 16-mob cap about 11 hostiles roam near spawn, and day is not the calm half of the loop. The zone tier (distance ring) changes only mob count and hostile share; health and damage are copied straight from MOB_TYPES at every tier. A level-10 player at the world's edge fights the same 100 HP husk as at spawn, and a 220 HP, 25-damage moss brute can spawn beside a level-1 player in minute one. The duskhound 'pack hunter', with per-id flank sides, always spawns alone.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/systems/SpawnerSystem.jsx:38-70,150-160; frontend/src/systems/spawnPlacement.js (28-85 m); frontend/src/game/dayNight.js:90-133; frontend/src/game/mobTypes.js:7-18 (weights); frontend/src/game/mobMovement.js:17-19
findings.proposal: Add game/encounters.js, a self-contained table of authored groups keyed by (zoneTier, biome, day/night). Examples: tier 0 by day, a lone husk, 3 skitterlings, or passives; tier 1, a hound pack of 3 (they split, since flank sides are already hashed) or 2 skeletons screened by a husk; tier 2+, a 'camp' of brute and 2 husks idling around a small stamp until aggro'd. Brutes only at tier 1+ or at night. Elite affix on tier 2+ spawns: 'Ember-touched' gets +60% HP, a rim glow through the existing per-instance rimColor, a burning zone on death through elementZones, and double loot and XP. Spawn each group around one anchor and keep the existing maxMobs caps. This also gives the heavy something to break if a guard mob is added (R2 runner-up P3). Gates: a unit test on the table. A seeded spawner unit asserts 0 brutes near spawn by day and more than 0 elites at tier 3. A probe counts group sizes in a running world.

findings.title: The night siege is announced like a set piece but plays as +4 to a spawn cap
findings.observation: Nightfall sounds a horn and posts 'Night 1 — the first siege begins. Hold until dawn!'. Mechanically, night 1 raises the cap from 16 to 20 and the hostile share from about 70% to about 93% of the same random trickle, centred on wherever the player stands. Nothing marches on the Hearth or on anything the player built. Walls matter only if the player happens to stand behind them, and nothing peaks, climaxes or ends early across the 150 s night.

findings.proposal: Add a siege director, a self-contained scheduler with a 15 Hz bridge. At the horn it picks 1-2 bearings, shown as red compass wedges and a horizon glow. Waves spawn at 0 s, 45 s and 95 s from the treeline 40-60 m out, using the encounter table at night tier. They head for the nearer of the Hearth and the player's latest placed-block cluster (the worker only needs targetX/Z). The third wave is led by a named captain elite carrying a banner; killing it ends the siege early with the dawn-style payoff. Night N scales wave size and elite count. This gives 'bank by day, spend at night' a set piece to spend on, and later works with R2's lantern spawn suppression. Gates: a scheduler unit (wave times, size ramp, captain in wave 3). An e2e forces night and asserts spawns arrive within 30 degrees of the chosen bearing and that a captain kill ends the siege.

findings.title: In first person, attacks from behind give no warning, and every mob's windup is the same 380 ms
findings.observation: Windups show only on the mob's own mesh (a coil pose and an emissive ramp). There is no audio tell; the sound API has no mob windup voice. DamageDirection lights red only after a hit lands. A hound or skitterling behind the player cannot be read, so the perfect dodge only works against what is on screen. Every mob uses the default WINDUP_MS of 380 ms, whether it is a 5-damage skitterling or a 25-damage brute. In perfect-dodge-windup.png the winding husk fills the screen at point blank, so the coil cannot be read as a pose.

findings.proposal: (a) Add a 15 Hz HUD reader beside DamageDirection, reusing its screen-perimeter math. It draws an amber chevron at the screen edge for any mob within 8 m that is winding up outside the view cone. AIWorkerSystem already passes windupUntil back. (b) Add a spatialised windup voice per archetype through synthVoices: a hiss for skitterlings, a grunt for husks, a deep inhale for brutes. (c) Add windupMs to mobArchetypes: skitterling 260, hound 320, husk 380, spider leap 450, brute 620. The worker passes it to attackPhase, and the perfect-dodge window scales as a fraction of it. Gates: a unit test where an in-view mob draws no chevron and a mob behind the player draws one. A worker test asserts the brute's windup is 620 ms. An e2e plants a windup behind the player and expects the chevron, with an in-view control that shows none.

findings.title: The beast form shows the beast for 1.2 s, then plays its 14 s in first person
findings.observation: transformCam holds the third-person reveal for 1.2 s and then returns to first person for the rest of the 14 s form. So the player spends the game's biggest power fantasy as a camera with damage multipliers, never seeing the comet, bull, hawk or golem they banked 7 kills to become. beast-fire.png shows how well it reads from behind. SOTA-INITIATIVE records third-person as Kevin's direction, with the control pivot deferred.

findings.proposal: Keep the transformCam pose (MAX_DIST 4.5, RISE_Y 1.0) for the whole form. Pull the camera in on collision with a Rapier ray cast from head to camera. Take the aim and melee cone from the avatar's position, with facing set to camera yaw. Return to first person on exit through the existing envelope. This is the first step of Kevin's recorded third-person direction, limited to 14 s windows, so the aim and control risks are measured before any full pivot. Gates: an e2e roar asserts the camera stays at least 3 m from the avatar for the form's duration and first person is restored on exit. A melee cone hit from third person lands on a husk in front of the avatar. Capture mode is untouched, since forms never appear in captures.

findings.title: Shrines do not do what their lore promises, so exploration has no goal ladder
findings.observation: Old Pike tells the player 'Each [shrine] we reclaim weakens the Blight Heart'. Nothing implements it: no reclaim or lit state exists anywhere in src. A shrine is a landmark mesh plus one guaranteed chest. Reaching any shrine completes 'pilgrim' once, and after that shrines have no further purpose on the way to the climax.

findings.proposal: 'Light the shrine': pressing G at a shrine starts a 45 s hold-the-light event, two waves from the encounter table at that shrine's tier. Success lights a beam (the existing landmark emissive plus bloom) and increments a saved shrinesLit count. Each lit shrine, up to 3, strips 10% of the dragon's HP and removes one of its tricks (shrine 2 ends the skeleton summons), and the compass announces it. Unlit shrines show dim on the compass. This gives a skilled player a reason to go further and an underpowered player a way to make the climax fair. Gates: a unit test on bossTierStats with shrinesLit. An e2e completes the event and asserts the dragon spawns with less HP; a failed event (player leaves the radius) changes nothing.

findings.title: No build identity: every capstone and affix is a flat stat, and one character owns all four Aspects by about level 9
findings.observation: The 'mutually exclusive' capstones are stat sticks: Singularity +8 STR against Event Horizon +14 Armor; Apex Predator +8 STR against Untamed +10 AGI; the same for Soulbind and Elemancer. All six affixes are flat stats. With one talent point per level and two points per Aspect unlock, a level-9 character owns all four signature verbs. Player-facing text leaks implementation: 'stay feral longer (read at the duration timer, not the stat-fold)' is visible in progression-open.png.

findings.proposal: Make each capstone pair change a verb, Hades-boon style, at read sites that already exist. Singularity: a hurled block implodes on impact (pulls mobs within 4 m, 1 s stun). Event Horizon: a perfect dodge while holding a block auto-hurls it at the staggered mob. Apex Predator: kills in beast form extend the form 2 s. Untamed: the beast form's dodge leaves its element zone. Communion: bound allies' hits apply your loaded spell's secondary. Bulwark: allies taunt. Conflux: Imbue paints two zone kinds. Wildfire: burning zones spread to one adjacent mob. Add 6 legendary affixes on verb hooks (on perfect dodge, on heavy release, on kill inside a zone). Strip the dev-speak from the descriptions. Gates: one unit test per capstone at its read site; an e2e for Singularity's pull.

findings.title: Light melee is the same swing every time: no string, no finisher, no commitment
findings.observation: Every tap throws the same 90 degree cone on a 300 ms cooldown at full walk speed, and nothing in src tracks a combo step. The heavy covered the held half of R2's 'click-spam' finding, but the tap rhythm, which is most of the attacks a player makes, has no shape.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/Components.jsx:150,218-319; docs/superpowers/sota-2026-09/EXTERNAL-BASELINE-R2.md:50
findings.proposal: Add game/meleeString.js, a self-contained 3-step light string. Steps 1 and 2 are today's swing. Step 3 is a 140 degree sweep at 1.5x with knockback and the 'heavy' hitstop tier. The string resets after 650 ms without input. Each swing slows the walk to 0.6x for 120 ms, a commitment that the combat-stance change makes meaningful. The FPV hand arc alternates direction each step (the ribbon already exists). A heavy hold still suppresses taps, as today. Gates: a unit test on step thresholds and reset. An e2e with real clicks asserts the third hit deals 1.5x and reaches a mob at 60 degrees off-axis that step 1 misses.

findings.title: Element chemistry punishes combining: fire and ice delete each other, and zones ignore the other Aspects
findings.observation: When a burning zone touches a frozen one, spawnZone deletes both and returns null, so the only cross-element interaction erases both effects. Zones never interact with hurled Voidhand blocks, beast forms, Soulbind allies or storms. Resonant zones only set isAggro. The BotW/TotK bar is that systems combine into payoffs.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/game/elementZones.js:16-22,35-43 (annihilate), :100-128 (applyZoneEffects)
findings.proposal: Add a reaction table with payoffs, keeping MAX_ZONES as the performance cap. Burning plus frozen makes steam: a 2.5 m, 4 s cloud where mobs lose aggro and their windups cancel. A frozen (slowed) mob hit by a heavy or a hurl shatters for +100% damage. A conductive zone in a storm (weatherGate) gets 1.5x radius. A Voidhand block hurled through a burning zone becomes a flaming projectile that ignites its target. A beast form standing in its own element's zone gains +20% damage. Gates: a unit test per reaction; an e2e where steam cancels a planted windup.

findings.title: Dungeons are empty rooms
findings.observation: 2.5% of chunks stamp a 13x13 stone room with wood pillars and a sand 'Treasure block' on a snow 'marble' altar. Nothing places a chest, a mob or any reward there; no consumer in QuestSystem or the spawners references dungeons. A player who finds one gets an empty box. That is the worst outcome for a 'reason to explore'.

findings.title: Quests are counters handed out by a list, not by the NPCs
findings.observation: Quests are auto-assigned counters in list order: place 20 blocks, break 30, cast 10 spells, defeat 50, then endless 'Bounty N: kill 15+5n'. The NPC 'givers' are only a lore string; pressing G on Pike says one fixed line. Two quests name mobs the game calls something else: 'Defeat 10 zombies' (Husk) and 'Defeat 25 skeletons' (Bonepicker). The authored story order was deleted because nothing read it.

The beats: Pike, survive the Prologue. Mara, forge a stone sword from mined stone, which gives mining a purpose. Wren, hold the Hearth through the first siege. Pike, light the first shrine. Bram, kill the camp captain. Pike, the Blight Heart. Keep counters as optional bounties on Bram's board. Fix the mob names through MOB_TYPES displayName. Gates: a unit test that the chain order is what quest offering reads (one source). An e2e completes beat 1 and receives beat 2 only after G on Mara.

findings.title: Death costs nothing, so a night siege carries no tension
findings.observation: Respawn restores full HP, mana and hunger and keeps everything. The only cost is the walk back from spawn, which takes seconds at 14 m/s. 'Soft death' is a decision of record, so stakes must stay soft.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx:1002-1011; SOTA-INITIATIVE.md:150 (soft death); frontend/src/world/survivalSystem.js:31-40 (meters bleed at dawn)
findings.proposal: Keep death soft. On death, drop the banked Aspect meters (Ferocity, Kinetic, Soul, Resonance) and carried coins into an 'ember cache' at the death site, marked on the compass and minimap. Touching it restores them; dying again before recovering forfeits the old cache. No items or XP are lost. The night's power becomes something to protect without a punitive penalty. Gates: a unit test on cache create and recover. An e2e asserts that dying with a full Ferocity bank leaves a cache, touching it restores 100, and a second death replaces it.

summary: Crafty's engine and feel systems are well past hobby grade: vertex AO, clouds with cloud shadows, the far-field horizon, the GPU ocean, world hitstop and the perfect dodge have all shipped. Its frames still do not read as one authored art direction, because the look is assembled from defaults that work against each other. There are three large gaps. First, light and colour: night is a sunset frozen in place with no key light, every shadow is a saturated cobalt or teal because a saturated-blue ambient light does the shadow work, and bloom catches the whole sky. Second, surfaces: textures are white noise at the scale of single texels, grass hills are green on every face, untextured toon props stand beside textured terrain, and every pond runs a smooth, plastic-looking storm swell. Third, characters and VFX: mobs are one-colour boxes that flatten into flat stickers at the exact moment they telegraph, the Shadow Dragon is a box, and spells read as pastel confetti. Most of the highest-leverage fixes are palette, shader-constant and data changes that cost nothing on the GPU, so the heat budget on the M3 Max and iPad is not what holds the look back; taste and an honest view of the real game are. The honest view is currently missing: the 31 baseline frames are rendered in software (SwiftShader), were captured before the clouds and far field shipped, run with motion off and include no iPad frame, so every finding below should be accepted against a set of real-GPU, motion-on screenshots that includes iPad viewports.

findings.title: Night is a sunset frozen in place, with no key light and a painted moon
findings.observation: The colour script is keyed to the isDay boolean, not to the sun. sampleMood takes the sky, sun, fog and ambient colours from the mood value only; the day cycle only rotates the sun's direction. When isDay flips, the sky lerps to the dusk palette in about 1.5 s (lerp rate delta*2.0) and then holds it all night: horizon #C25A3A red-orange, sun #FF8A4C, fog #3A2E40. So dawn and sunset never play out as events; the day is noon-blue from dawn to dusk and the whole night is orange-magenta, with every surface in one hue family (explore-night.png: maroon tree silhouettes, brick-red terrain, an orange glow blob at screen centre). Between cycle 0.5 and 1 the orange sun sits below the horizon and still runs at intensity 0.85, with no horizon gate. The moon is a disc painted at a fixed direction in the sky shader and casts no light. In real play, then, the night has no key light and no cast shadows; terrain is lit only by flat ambient plus the hemisphere light. The capture pins the sun at noon (CAPTURE_SOLAR_FRACTION 0.25), so the explore-night baseline shows an orange-sunlit night that no player ever sees.

findings.proposal: Drive colour by sun elevation instead of the boolean. Build a six-key colour script indexed by cycleFraction (dawn pink-gold, morning, noon, golden hour, blue hour, moonlit night). Apply the danger mood as an overlay on that script (a red horizon tint and denser fog during a siege), not as the base night. When the sun crosses the horizon, hand the SAME directional light to the moon: colour about #9DB4FF, intensity about 0.35, on its own arc opposite the sun, shadows kept on. This adds no light and so causes no shader relink. The night sky becomes deep blue-violet with stars, and stays warm near the horizon only at the sunset azimuth during blue hour. This pairs with R2 #5 (lantern plus baked block light, queued, not built): warm local pools only read against a cool night. To verify, add a non-capture probe at cycle 0.30, 0.48, 0.55 and 0.75 with the frames opened, plus a gate that the key-light direction stays above the horizon around the clock.

findings.title: Every shadow is saturated cobalt or teal, and nothing bounces warm
findings.observation: The ambient light is skyMid at intensity 0.9; in explore that is #2E8AE0, a saturated blue. The hemisphere light's ground colour is the fog colour (#CFEAF2, pale cyan), and the vertex-AO floor is also tinted by the sky, so no light anywhere bounces warm. Pixels sampled from the baselines: shadow on snow is rgb(35,86,138) next to lit snow at about rgb(137,155,193), so the shadow pools read as water (biome-snow.png). Cast shadows on sand go to deep teal, rgb(7,54,61) and rgb(17,51,54), against lit sand at rgb(130,137,125) (ocean-coast.png). As a result every one-block step draws a dark teal contour line, and the coast reads as a topographic map rather than sunlit ground. The flat 0.9 ambient also flattens form on faces that are not in shadow.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/render/mood.js:25 (explore ambientIntensity 0.90), :61 (ROLE ambient = skyMid), and the COL hemiGround = PALETTE.fog assignment; frontend/src/world/Terrain.jsx:171 (sky-coloured AO floor); pixel samples from tests/visual/baseline/biome-snow.png at (620,470) and ocean-coast.png at (780,450) and (900,600)
findings.proposal: Re-balance the light rig. Drop the flat ambient to about 0.25 and move that energy into the hemisphere light, with a desaturated sky colour (around #8FB4D8) and a warm ground bounce keyed per mood (warm olive over grass, ochre over sand; one colour per mood is enough). In the terrain's lights_fragment_end patch, where the cloud shadow already sits, add a shadowTint uniform that pulls shadowed direct light toward an authored colour, so shadow colour is designed rather than a by-product of the ambient. Target shadows cooler, about 40% darker and LESS saturated than lit ground: shadow/lit luminance about 0.55, with shadow chroma below lit chroma. Check with same-renderer A/B frames of hearth, biome-snow and ocean-coast.

findings.title: Terrain textures are per-texel white noise, grass cliffs are green on all sides, and props use a different art language
findings.observation: Every block layer is a 32x32 texture filled with sin-hash noise that has no correlation between neighbouring texels. Grass flips 35% of texels darker; leaves flip 15% to near-black 'holes'. Up close this reads as TV static: leaves look like mouldy, black-speckled cubes (left side of mipmaps-ab-biome-snow.png and mipmaps-ab-hearth-grass.png). At range it crawls into moire, because mipmaps are built but switched off. The texture layer is simply the block type, with no distinction between top and side faces. Grass hills are therefore green cliffs with no dirt band under the turf lip, snow blocks are white on every side, and terraces lose their strata (hearth.png, the left slopes of explore-day.png). Meanwhile huts, stalls and walls are flat, untextured toon boxes with 3-5 px ink outlines (the hut in beast-*.png, the red wall in perfect-dodge-windup.png), and the water is a smooth glossy sheet. One frame mixes three render languages.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/world/proceduralTextures.js:48-66 (getNoise; grass isFoliage n1>0.65), :132-135 (leaves isHole), :19 (TERRAIN_MIPMAPS=false); frontend/src/world/Terrain.jsx:129-134 (layerIndex = vBlockType); docs/superpowers/sota-2026-09/evidence/mipmaps-ab-biome-snow.png, mipmaps-ab-hearth-grass.png; tests/visual/baseline/hearth.png, beast-fire.png
findings.proposal: Re-author the 16 layers as structured bold-flat pixel art. They stay procedural and free: 2-4 clustered tones in low-frequency shapes. Grass: blade clumps and a lighter top rim. Stone: 3-4 chunky facets with 1 px cracks. Leaves: clustered lobes with a lit upper edge and no black holes. Sand: soft ripples. Wood: rings on top faces, bark lines on side faces. Add per-face selection in the terrain shader: grass and snow side faces sample dirt or stone with a 3-4 texel turf or snow cap taken from fract(vWorldPos.y), using the world-space face normal (the mesher already knows dirFlag). Turn on TERRAIN_MIPMAPS (built, with an A/B already in KEVIN-REVIEW-BATCH). Give the voxelKit props the same palette through a small atlas, or through per-face two-tone vertex colour plus the terrain's per-block jitter, so buildings and terrain share one material grammar while keeping the ink outline.

findings.title: Mobs flatten into stickers at the moment they telegraph, and vanish against the night
findings.observation: Mobs are single-colour boxes with a 2-band toon ramp and a 5 px near-black outline. In character-closeup.png the body is one flat green, the eyes are two red squares, and the outline breaks at the joints. The windup telegraph adds #ff3a00 emissive at up to 1.5 over the whole body, and the hit flash sets both body and emissive to white at 1.5 for 300 ms. So at exactly the moments that matter, the mob loses all shading and reads as a flat salmon or white cut-out (perfect-dodge-windup.png). The bestiary palette is dark (navy spider, aubergine wolf, forest-green brute in mob-bestiary.png), the outline is near-black, and the fresnel rim runs on the high tier only. At night on iPad's low tier, mobs therefore dissolve into dark terrain except for their eyes, and the night siege is where combat happens.

findings.proposal: (1) Telegraph through the edge, not the body. The windup ramps the rim strength and the per-instance outline colour toward danger red while the body keeps its toon shading. The hit flash becomes 60-80 ms of white on the lit band plus a white outline, then a 3-frame squash. (2) Turn the rim on at every tier (one dot product on a handful of meshes) with a mood-driven colour, cool moon-white at night. (3) Author 2-3 tones of part detail as data: a lighter face or belly plate, darker hands and feet, and one strap or band per archetype; give the eyes HDR emissive so they bloom once the bloom finding lands. (4) Optionally lift the outline value at night so silhouettes separate from dark ground.

findings.title: Spell VFX are pastel confetti on a bright sky, and each cast changes the scene's light count
findings.observation: In the spell baselines, projectiles are small pastel shapes. The fireball's pale lavender ellipse halo reads as a sticker, lightning is a 2 px lavender line, and impacts are sprinkles of pink and white specks. On a bright sky the additive layers almost disappear, and there is no ground interaction (no scorch, frost or smoke). Each projectile and each impact also mounts its own pointLight. This repo already records that a light-count change re-links every lit shader program and causes a one-frame hitch, and that is why the voidhand keeps its light permanently mounted. Combat VFX are therefore a hitch source exactly when the frame matters most.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/render/spellVfx.jsx:434 and :618 (pointLight per projectile and per impact); frontend/src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:488-493 (one component per projectile and impact); frontend/src/world/PhantomBlockSystem.jsx:18-20 (light-count change re-links every program); tests/visual/baseline/spell-cast.png, spell-lightning.png, spell-arcane.png, spell-iceball.png
findings.proposal: Adopt a bold-flat VFX grammar. Each element gets a SOLID saturated core with an ink outline (normal blend, so it reads on any sky), one additive glow shell, and a dark secondary for contrast (fire smoke, ice mist, arcane void). Impacts get an expanding ground-ring decal, a short-lived scorch or frost decal, 6-10 chunky voxel debris cubes from the existing GPUSparkSystem, and a shock ring. Scale everything up about 1.5x. Replace the per-VFX pointLights with a pool of 4 always-mounted lights that are assigned each frame to the brightest live effects, at intensity 0 when unused, so the light count never changes.

findings.title: Bloom catches the whole sky, and the grade pushes saturation everywhere
findings.observation: Bloom's luminanceThreshold is 0.65 on a HalfFloat HDR buffer (the default frameBufferType in @react-three/postprocessing 3.0.4). That sits below the sky dome's horizon luminance, so the sky, snow, foam and motes bloom every frame and halo over the treeline: the horizon in explore-day.png is a milky white wall, and OVERNIGHT records the ground under the horizon going about 8 levels darker once bright sky stopped blooming over it. This contradicts tokens.js, which names the MAGIC palette as 'the ONLY intended bloom sources'. The grade then adds +0.30 saturation globally on an already saturated palette. Measured on a crop that excludes the HUD, mean HSV saturation is 0.55 to 0.65 on the day and hearth frames. Highlights top out around 220/255 under NEUTRAL tone mapping, so snow and cloud tops never reach white.

findings.proposal: Raise the bloom threshold above 1.0 and make bloom a deliberate signal: VFX cores, mob eyes, the sun disc, the parked ore glow and the future lantern carry HDR emissive above 1 (most already set toneMapped=false). In the existing HueSaturation and BrightnessContrast slot, or in one small custom Effect in the same EffectPass (no new pass), replace the global saturation boost with a per-mood split-tone: shadows lifted toward the mood's shadow hue, warmer highlights, and saturation scaled by luminance so mid-tones stay rich and darks desaturate. Re-tune exposure so snow and cloud tops reach about 245.

findings.title: The water is one storm swell everywhere, a plastic-looking sheet with no depth and no underwater
findings.observation: A single 220 m Gerstner plane, with about 2 m of summed amplitude at steepness 1.0, runs the same open-ocean swell in every inlet and below-sea-level valley. Foam starts at a crest height of 0.85 m, so mid-distance water reads as stepped white terraces, like snowfields (centre of explore-day.png), and the open sea bulges above the coastline as a smooth glossy hump covered in white flecks (ocean-coast.png). It reads as liquid plastic that ignores the block grammar. There is no depth colour: the shallow-to-deep tint lived in the old voxel-water path, which has been gone since W2. ocean-depth.png, an underwater camera pose, shows a dry-looking seabed in black-blue noise with the sea surface as a ribbon in the sky. The audio muffles underwater, but the picture does not change.

findings.proposal: On each ocean recentre, bake a 96x96 seabed-depth DataTexture over the plane from the same surface formula (climate.surfaceBlockAt). The cost is CPU work on recentre only, plus one texture fetch per fragment. Use it to (a) scale wave amplitude by depth, so water is calm up to about 3 m deep and the full swell runs only offshore; (b) give the water 3 toon depth bands (turquoise, teal, navy) with a crisp foam line where depth reaches 0; and (c) aim the Fresnel at the analytic sky-gradient colour instead of a fixed teal. Below sea level: underwater fog in teal, a screen tint, and a moving caustic term on the seabed, built the same way as the existing cloud-shadow hook.

findings.title: The title screen hides its best asset under the wordmark and a black scrim

Acceptance: a solid-black 64 px silhouette is recognisably a dragon.

findings.title: Grass sits on a 2-block grid, and every chunk has a bald strip
findings.observation: grassTops places tufts on a fixed lattice of every second block and returns as soon as it reaches cap 50 in z-major scan order. A full grass chunk has 64 candidate spots, so its last 14 positions (half of row z=12 and all of row z=14) never get grass. That leaves a bald strip along the +z edge of every all-grass chunk, repeating chunk by chunk, and every tuft stands on an exact grid point. Each tuft is one flat-colour 0.4x0.7 rectangle. From player height the meadow reads as sparse dark ticks; from above it reads as rotated green paper squares (mipmaps-ab-hearth-grass.png). The ground texture's noise ends up doing the work the grass should do.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/world/grassField.js:46-58 (stride 2, cap 50, early return); frontend/src/OptimizedGrassSystem.jsx:265 (planeGeometry 0.4x0.7); docs/superpowers/sota-2026-09/evidence/mipmaps-ab-hearth-grass.png; tests/visual/baseline/explore-day.png
findings.proposal: Jitter placement with a per-column hash, and spread the cap evenly by reservoir-sampling the candidates instead of truncating the scan. Replace the rectangle with a crossed 3-blade tuft with tapered tips. Colour it from root to tip: the root takes the ground's grass colour times AO so tufts grow out of the turf, and the tip takes a warm sunlit lime; add per-instance height and hue jitter. Spend the instance budget by distance ring (dense near, faded out by about 25 m) at the same total count. The low tier keeps today's caps.

findings.title: Light motes read as dust on the lens, including a blob at screen centre

Every daytime frame therefore has 15-25 white orbs scattered over open sky (explore-day, landmark, ocean-coast). A mote close to the camera lands as a large glare blob next to the crosshair, at the same pixel in explore-day, explore-night and boss-obsidian, tinted white, orange or red by the mood. findings.title: The sky and distance flatten into a milky wall: a gradient stripe, cloud streaks and a stretched moon

summary: Crafty is on the right side of the 2026 line architecturally: it renders WebGL2 through R3F and already has baked voxel AO, clouds with shadows, a far field, world-wide hitstop, a perfect dodge and heavy melee. The rendering stack is out of date, though: three is 14 minors behind (0.172 against 0.186.1) and @react-three/postprocessing is at 3.0.4 against 3.2.2. The newer releases fix defects Crafty has run into: the composer being rebuilt on every render, the composer not resizing when the pixel ratio changes, and the production WebGL error storm. All peer dependency ranges allow the upgrade today. One mechanism found here can corrupt rendering on iPad and Safari: each quality-tier step changes the canvas pixel ratio, and the installed postprocessing composer does not follow that change, so N8AO ambient occlusion and the composer's buffers run at the wrong resolution. Moving to WebGPU/TSL is not worth it now. The three.js manual still calls WebGPURenderer experimental, Safari 26.x has shipped WebGPU regressions on iPad, and the migration would replace the whole post-processing chain; the right time is when R3F v10 goes stable. The biggest levers on looks are free to run: baked sky light plus block light with a time-of-day lookup texture (the recipe Minecraft presented at GDC 2026) and fog that glows toward the sun. The biggest lever on feel is replacing the fully synthesized sound effects with layered CC0 recordings. Heat is best cut by a pixel budget, a GPU-time governor on Chromium, and shadow maps that update only when something changed.

findings.title: iPad/Safari: the post-processing composer keeps a stale resolution after every quality-tier step
findings.observation: The Canvas pixel ratio depends on the quality tier: dpr={[1, q.dprCap]}, with dprCap 1.5 at low and 2 at med/high. An iPad always starts at low (coarse pointer). Safari on a Mac also starts at low, because Safari does not implement navigator.deviceMemory, so selectTier reads 0. The governor's first step from low to med therefore changes the drawing-buffer ratio from 1.5 to 2. The installed @react-three/postprocessing 3.0.4 resizes the composer only when the CSS size changes (`useEffect(()=>composer.setSize(size.width,size.height),[composer,size])`), so the composer's buffers and N8AO pass stay at the old ratio. Upstream issue #280 shows the symptom: N8AO paints ghost reflections of other objects after a pixel-ratio change. The same holds in reverse on an M3 Max: stepping down to low (ratio 2 to 1.5) leaves the composer at the larger size, and PR #381 measured that stale state at 3.03 ms against 0.83 ms of composer GPU time. The heat-saving step therefore saves less than it should. Separately, <AdaptiveDpr pixelated> never acts, because nothing calls performance.regress() (grep finds 0 calls).

findings.title: Heat: cap the render at a pixel budget instead of a fixed pixel ratio, and govern by GPU time where the browser exposes it
findings.observation: The high tier renders at pixel ratio 2. On a full-screen 16-inch M3 Max that is about 7.7 Mpx through roughly 7 full-screen passes (quality.js's own comment). The tier governor reads only frame rate; the GameScene comment admits a machine pinned at 100% GPU while holding 60 fps never steps down. Minecraft's GDC 2026 talk names high-resolution screens as probably the largest mobile performance factor. It renders Vibrant Visuals on its Tier 2 iOS devices at 480p (60 fps in Performance mode, 30 fps in Visuals mode), and warns that thermal throttling destroys performance in a non-recoverable way and that keeping frame rates at 30 fps leaves headroom. EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 (GPU timer queries) is available in Chrome/Edge 70 and later but not in Safari on macOS or iOS.

findings.proposal: (1) Derive the pixel ratio from a pixel budget: dpr = min(dprCap, sqrt(budget / cssPixels)), with a budget around 3.5-4 Mpx at high and about 2 Mpx at low. That halves the fill on a 16-inch MacBook Pro and leaves a laptop at 1x unchanged. Take the next finding's call on the budget rather than the old dprCap debate (T11). Add react-postprocessing 3.2's Sharpness effect at low strength if the image softens. (2) On Chromium, wrap composer.render in a timer query and step the tier down when p90 GPU time exceeds about 8 ms under the 60 fps cap, keeping frame rate as Safari's signal. (3) Measure the result in watts: run `sudo powermetrics --samplers gpu_power` for 5 minutes of idle play per change, before and after; that is the metric Kevin's fans respond to.

findings.title: Looks and play: bake sky light and block light per vertex, then shade through a time-of-day lookup texture (the Minecraft 2026 recipe)
findings.observation: Crafty has no light field: grep for blockLight, skyLight and lightLevel finds 0. Caves, overhangs and building interiors get the same ambient light and sky fill as open ground, darkened only by vertex AO and the sun shadow map. Round two proposed a lantern with block light (its #5), and it is not built; it is not among the parked features. The GDC 2026 slides add three things that proposal lacked. First, sky light (0-15, from the heightmap plus flood fill, bleeding up to 15 steps around corners) stands for indirect light: the talk calls it free global illumination that lights cave mouths correctly. Second, both channels are baked into each vertex and looked up in a 2D brightness texture (x = block light, y = sky light) that is regenerated per time of day and dimension, so day/night/boss grading costs one texture fetch. Third, coloured block light comes from propagating each light-source type separately, with SWAR bit-packing (several small additions done in one 32-bit word).

findings.proposal: In the terrain worker, compute a sky-light BFS seeded from the column heightmap and a block-light BFS seeded from emissive blocks. Pack both into one byte per vertex (4+4 bits), include it in the greedy-merge key (the AO lesson), and cross chunk borders. In the terrain shader, sample a 16×16 LUT DataTexture that the mood driver rewrites when the time of day or the boss sky changes. Add a craftable lantern full-cube block using the parked emissive-ore path, and a spawn rule: no hostile spawns at light 8 or above. Optionally, for the hearth only, bake LightProbeGridWebGL once for coloured bounce light, available after the r186 bump. Gates: worker units (15 at the source, 14 one step away, stopped by stone, continuous across a two-chunk fixture), a mesher fixture where a floor next to a lantern makes at least 2 quads, a night capture A/B of a lit base, and remesh time on fixed seeds (Q51) within budget.

findings.title: Looks: make the fog glow toward the sun and integrate height fog analytically
findings.observation: The fog is a single colour mixed by a factor that is multiplied by the fragment's own world height (Atmosphere.jsx:79-89); there is no sun term, although the resolved sun direction already exists (Atmosphere.jsx:279-280). explore-day.png shows the result: a flat, washed-out haze over the middle distance, with nothing marking where the light comes from. Inigo Quilez's fog article gives near-free fixes that need no extra pass. Tint the fog toward a warm sun colour by pow(max(dot(viewDir, sunDir), 0), 8). Split extinction and in-scattering into separate RGB coefficients. Use the analytic exponential height-fog integral (one division), so that looking down through thin air stays clear while the horizon thickens.

findings.proposal: Extend the patched fog chunks with a world-position varying (vec3 instead of vFogWorldY) plus uniforms for sun direction and sun-fog colour. Mood drives them: warm at dawn and dusk, pale by day, a cold moon tint at night, sickly in the boss sky. Replace the per-point heightMul with the analytic integral. Cost per fragment: one dot product, one pow, one division. Gates: a compiled-program gate showing the term is linked into the terrain, water and far-field programs; a same-renderer A/B facing toward and away from the sun, where the sun-facing horizon must gain warmth and UI pixels must change 0.000%; a mutation zeroing the sun term must turn the A/B red.

findings.title: Frame rate facts the cap must honour: Safari already runs at 60, iOS Low Power Mode runs at 30

summary: I checked the plan's verified claims against the source and they hold. The composer's pass-building layout effect depends on its children, and three r172 allocates a light's shadow map only when it is null (WebGLShadowMap.js:140). The memo, the 60 fps cap and the shadow reset are on local main, but none of them is live: origin/main is still 57c45ae4. None of the three touches what most likely still heats the 120 Hz M3 Max. At dpr 2 the canvas is about 7 Mpx, and every pixel goes through a full-resolution half-float chain (render, N8AO, an effect pass with GodRays and Bloom, SMAA, then tone mapping). On top of that, four DOM requestAnimationFrame loops run outside the cap at the display rate, the shadow map is re-rendered every frame, and the world keeps drawing at 60 fps behind panels and while the player is idle. For the iPad, the strongest mechanism I found is the tier governor. Under the cap, 60 fps always looks like headroom, so it keeps stepping up until a tier fails and then steps back down (roughly a 5-second loop), and each step changes nine settings at once. On top of that, the GodRays and N8AO effects are never disposed, and nothing in the app reads the context-loss flag, so a lost context leaves a black or frozen canvas. The comment in GameScene saying the bounds' dead zone prevents oscillation is wrong in exactly this case. The biggest gap against a 2026 bar is measurement: nothing reports GPU time per pass, GPU power, or what an actual iPad does. A render-resolution pixel budget, governor hysteresis, effect disposal plus a recovery screen, and on-device diagnostics are all small-to-medium jobs and should come before any new effects.

findings.title: Cap canvas resolution with a pixel budget: about 1.5 / 1.25 / 1.0 dpr on the M3 Max, not 2 / 2 / 1.5
findings.observation: The canvas uses dpr [1, q.dprCap], with dprCap 2 at high and med and 1.5 at low. The M3 Max reports devicePixelRatio 2, so the canvas renders 3456x2234 = 7.72 Mpx fullscreen (about 6.9 Mpx windowed). The composer uses HalfFloat buffers (8 B/px) and runs RenderPass, then N8AO, then an EffectPass (GodRays + HueSat + BrightnessContrast + Bloom), then SMAA as its own convolution pass with two RGBA8 intermediates, then an EffectPass (ToneMapping + Noise + Vignette). That is roughly 5 full-resolution RGBA16F surfaces read and written per frame. My estimate (not measured) is 0.6 to 1 GB of memory traffic per frame, about 40 to 60 GB/s at the 60 cap, all of it scaling with dpr squared. The HUD is DOM, so it stays sharp at any canvas dpr. Block textures are 32x32 with nearest filtering, and a face is rarely more than 32 px on screen, so pixels above about 1.5 dpr mostly resample the same texel. The parked proposal of 2 to 1.75 cuts only 23% of pixels; 1.5 cuts 44%.

findings.proposal: Set the resolution from a pixel budget first, with the dpr cap as an upper bound: dpr = clamp(min(cap, devicePixelRatio, sqrt(budgetPx / (cssW*cssH))), 1, cap). Suggested values: high 4.2 Mpx / cap 1.75; med 2.8 Mpx / cap 1.5; low 1.8 Mpx / cap 1.25. In the M3 Max window that works out to about 1.52 / 1.24 / 1.0. On an iPad Pro 11 it is 1.75 / 1.5 / 1.25. On a 5K external monitor high falls to about 1.07 instead of 14.7 Mpx. Make dpr the governor's first lever (see the governor finding). Proving instruments: (1) powermetrics with gpu_power and thermal samplers at a 1 s interval for 120 s on the production build, same scene, cap on, at dpr 2 / 1.75 / 1.5 / 1.25, recording mean GPU mW and thermal pressure; (2) GPU ms per frame from EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 in Chromium; (3) side-by-side crops from a non-capture run for the eye test.

findings.title: Under the frame cap the tier governor oscillates, and each step changes nine settings at once (the leading iPad suspect)
findings.observation: With the cap on, governorBounds returns [40, 55]. drei's PerformanceMonitor inclines when more than 7.5 of its 10 samples (250 ms each) are at or above the upper bound. A capped device that holds 60 fps at tier T always reads 60 >= 55, so it always inclines until it reaches a tier it cannot hold. If that tier reads below 40 it declines, the tier below reads 60 again, and it inclines 2.5 s later. That is a loop of roughly 5 s. The dead zone only stops oscillation when a tier happens to land inside [40, 55]. flipflops is Infinity, so it never stops. The iPad starts at 'low' (coarse pointer) and climbs. Each step changes: dpr 1.5 to 2 (every composer target reallocated); N8AO and GodRays mount or unmount (shader compiles, slow on Metal); the shadow map is rebuilt and its extent changes among +-40, +-56 and +-72; renderDistance 2/3/4; the far-field inner radius; the weather and mote buffers are remounted; outlineWorldEdge; and charRim. AdaptiveDpr is mounted but does nothing: nothing in src calls regress(), so performance.current stays at 1. The comment at GameScene.jsx:277-279 says the dead zone prevents steady-state oscillation, which is wrong in this case.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/render/FrameCap.jsx:42-45; frontend/node_modules/@react-three/drei/core/PerformanceMonitor.js (useFrame sampler: upperBounds.length > iterations*threshold leads to onIncline; flipflops = Infinity); frontend/node_modules/@react-three/drei/core/AdaptiveDpr.js (reads state.performance.current); grep 'regress' in frontend/src finds 0; frontend/src/GameScene.jsx:277-279,311-327; frontend/src/render/quality.js:42; frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx:97
findings.proposal: (a) Add asymmetric hysteresis: after a decline from tier T, block inclining back to T for 60 s, doubling on each repeat, and stop at the lower tier for the session after 2 declines. (b) Under a cap, incline only when there is measured headroom: time each advance() in FrameCap with performance.now() and require it to stay below 55% of the interval for the whole window, because frame rate cannot rise above the cap. (c) Separate the settings: step dpr continuously first (cheap, no shader compiles), then the post effects, and never change renderDistance at runtime on touch devices. (d) Drive AdaptiveDpr with regress() or delete it. Proving instruments: the tier timeline that the untracked scripts/visual/ipad-probe.mjs already records, run on the production build in WebKit, plus an on-device tier-change log. The metric is tier changes per minute after a 20 s warm-up: at most 1, and 0 after 60 s.

findings.title: GodRays is rebuilt on every PostFX render, and GodRays and N8AO are never disposed
findings.observation: In the @react-three/postprocessing wrapper, GodRays builds its effect with useMemo(() => new GodRaysEffect(camera, sun, props), [camera, props]). The props object is new on every render, and the effect is mounted as a primitive with dispose={null}. N8AO is mounted as a primitive too. R3F 9.5 never disposes primitives on unmount. Each GodRaysEffect allocates renderTargetA, renderTargetB, renderTargetLight and a KawaseBlurPass. N8AO's halfRes mode allocates an R32F + RGBA16F multiple-render-target plus half-float targets. three tracks GPU objects only in WeakMaps, so render targets that are not disposed are freed only if and when the JS garbage collector finalizes them. On local main, PostFX re-renders on every tier change and on each sunAboveHorizon flip (twice per day cycle). With the governor oscillating, every flip leaves a GodRaysEffect behind, and every low-to-med flip leaves an N8AOPostPass. On the live site, which has no memo, a new GodRaysEffect is built on every hunger and mana tick.

findings.proposal: Wrap N8AO and GodRays in local components that build the effect once (memoized on camera, scene and sun only), push prop changes through setters, and call dispose() in a useEffect cleanup. Keep both mounted and toggle them (pass.enabled, or the effect's blend function set to SKIP) for horizon and tier changes. That avoids the pass rebuild and the shader compile. Proving instrument: a DEV test hook that counts GodRaysEffect and N8AOPostPass constructions alongside renderer.info.memory.textures. Force 20 tier flips and 4 horizon flips; the counts must return to their warm baseline. Mutation check: delete the cleanup and the count must grow.

findings.title: Context loss is caught but nothing reads the flag, so the canvas goes black with no way back
findings.observation: GameScene listens for webglcontextlost, calls preventDefault and sets isWebGLContextLost. Nothing in src reads that flag; it appears only in the store definition. When iPad Safari drops the context (memory pressure, an app switch, the GPU watchdog), the result is a frozen or black canvas under a working HUD, with no way to recover. Memory pressure is plausible. My estimate at med on an iPad Pro 13 (dpr 2, 5.7 Mpx): drawing buffer about 45 MB times its swap chain; composer 2xRGBA16F about 91 MB plus 23 MB of depth; SMAA about 45 MB; N8AO about 50 MB; bloom and godrays about 40 MB; shadow map 8 to 32 MB; resident chunk geometry for up to 81 to 169 chunks. On the title screen there is also a second canvas (TitleDiorama) with antialias:true and alpha:true at dpr up to 2, which adds roughly 36 B/px of 4x MSAA color + depth (about 200 MB) while the game canvas renders behind it.

findings.proposal: (1) Add a context-lost panel derived from the store flag, following the same pattern as shouldShowResumeOverlay: 'Graphics were reset by the system - tap to resume', which autosaves and then reloads. (2) On loss, write a breadcrumb to localStorage (tier, dpr, canvas px, uptime, tier-change count) and show it in a Diagnostics panel on the next boot. This is free real-device telemetry. (3) Give TitleDiorama antialias:false or a dpr cap of 1.5, and unmount it completely after Start. The parked work caps only its frame rate. Proving instrument: a WebKit probe on the production build that calls WEBGL_lose_context loseContext() and then restoreContext(). Assert that the panel appears, and that frames draw again after restore.

findings.title: HUD DOM loops run at the display rate (120 Hz), outside the frame cap
findings.observation: FrameCap paces only the R3F loop. Four DOM loops run on their own requestAnimationFrame at the display rate. ObjectiveTracker sets textContent on two nodes every frame, and setting textContent replaces the text node, so style, layout and paint run every vsync. Compass rebuilds innerHTML every frame; the parked fix writes only on change, but it still rebuilds about 20 nodes every frame while the camera turns, because each marker's left:% changes. AbilityBar and, on iPad, TouchControlsSurface also run every frame. So even under the 60 cap, the page produces about 120 compositor frames per second on a ProMotion panel, compositing the roughly 7 Mpx canvas layer and the HUD each time, and the main thread runs style and layout at 120 Hz.

Make every DOM write write-on-change (compare the value first). Render compass markers as a fixed pool of persistent nodes moved with transform: translateX, which needs no layout. Proving instruments: a Chrome trace on the production build during idle play with the cap on, counting Layout and RecalculateStyle events per second and frames presented per second (targets: at most 60 presented, about 0 layouts while standing still); and a probe that wraps requestAnimationFrame to count callbacks per second per source.

findings.title: Shadow map re-renders every frame; the bias has no normal-bias term, so low-sun acne is likely at the iPad's starting tier
findings.observation: three's shadowMap.autoUpdate defaults to true, so the map (2048 squared at high) is rebuilt on every rendered frame. That includes every chunk mesh in the shadow box (up to 81 casters) and every mob part (about 19 meshes per mob, all castShadow), even though the terrain light changes only when the texel-snapped centre moves or the sun direction moves. The bias is -0.0001 with no normalBias. At the low tier (512 texels over 80 m, 0.156 m per texel), which is where the iPad starts, and at the low sun angles the sun arc now reaches at dawn and dusk, that is the classic setup for acne stripes on sunlit top faces. This is unconfirmed until a frame is opened.

While mobs are inside the shadow box, also update at 30 Hz. That takes the shadow pass from 60 to at most 30 per second. (b) Set normalBias to about 0.6 x the texel size per tier (0.09 / 0.065 / 0.04 m) and bias to -0.0005. (c) Let only a mob's body and head cast shadows. Proving instruments: wrap renderer.shadowMap.render to count shadow renders per second, plus a GPU timer around it; and an A/B at a non-capture dawn frame (sun elevation about 12 degrees) at the low tier, measured with a stripe metric (row-wise luminance variance on a flat sunlit face).

findings.title: Ocean foam, Fresnel and highlight are added after fog, so the square plane's edge shows against the sky
findings.observation: The Ocean shader adds its Fresnel tint, highlight band and foam after #include <dithering_fragment>. In three r172 that include comes after <fog_fragment>, so those terms are never fogged and never get the terrain's aerial haze. The 220 m plane therefore keeps a bright, foam-flecked edge at +-110 m in front of the fogged far-field water. In ocean-coast.png the sea ends in a ^-shaped silhouette, which is the square plane's corner against the sky. Separately, oceanVisibleNear runs the full climate surface function at 9 points every frame on the main thread, even when the player is standing still.

findings.title: Rain, fireflies and grass bending follow a player position rounded to whole metres and updated 5 times a second; clear weather still uploads every instance every frame
findings.observation: PositionTracker stores playerPosition rounded to whole metres, every 200 ms. WeatherSystem places every rain, snow and firefly instance relative to that value, and GrassWindDriver uses it as the player's bend source. So while walking at about 5 m/s, the rain cloud jumps about 1 m five times a second, and the grass around the player bends in 1 m steps at 5 Hz. No capture frame can show this, because capture mode freezes weather and the player. Separately, in clear weather (the common case) the loop still runs all 400 rain, 200 snow and the firefly instances through updateMatrix/setMatrixAt at scale 0, re-uploads the three instance buffers every frame, and issues three draws of empty instances. The parked work does not touch WeatherSystem.

findings.title: The world renders at 60 fps behind panels, in an unfocused window, and while the player is idle
findings.observation: The parked paceFor (on wip/perf-t3-features) slows only the title screen, to 10 fps. Everywhere else the world renders at the 60 cap: behind full-screen panels (inventory, crafting, talents), behind the pause scrim, with the window unfocused, and while the player stands idle. That matches the case of a laptop sitting with the game open. The plan defers the pause case as a gameplay decision, but slowing the frame rate does not change gameplay, because the simulation already steps by delta.

findings.title: Draw calls: about 30 per mob, one grass draw per chunk, and chunks in the hysteresis band still drawn
findings.observation: Each mob renders about 19 meshes, each with a drei <Outlines> (an extra mesh), and all cast shadows. That is roughly 30 main-pass draws and 19 shadow draws per mob. Nights allow up to 40 mobs, which is on the order of 1,200 main-pass and 760 shadow draws, plus one useFrame per mob. Grass is one InstancedMesh per chunk with at most 50 instances, so every visible chunk adds a draw. Chunks stay resident and drawn out to renderDistance+2. A moving player at high can therefore carry up to 169 chunk meshes against an 81-chunk tier box (at low, 81 against 25). WebKit's CPU cost per draw call is higher than Chromium's, so iPad nights are the worst case, and that drives the governor down.

That is about 6 draws per mob instead of about 31. (b) Grass: one world-level InstancedMesh (or BatchedMesh) with a slot allocator per chunk, so 1 draw total. (c) Set visible = false on resident chunks beyond renderDistance+0.5 and update the far-field mask to match. Proving instrument: gpu-cost-probe already reads renderer.info.render.calls; run it on the SIEGE_NIGHTS scenario on the production build and record draw calls and CPU ms per frame (Long Animation Frames API) before and after.

findings.title: N8AO and GodRays have never been timed; med (the tier an iPad climbs into) carries both at dpr 2
findings.observation: N8AO at quality 'medium' with halfRes (16 AO samples, 8 denoise samples per its preset) and GodRays at 60 samples and default 0.5 resolution scale run at both med and high. Together with SMAA and the mipmap bloom, they are the heaviest per-pixel shading cost on top of the bandwidth in the resolution finding. gpu-cost-probe reports draw calls, programs, textures and fps, but not GPU ms per pass, so nobody knows how much each one costs.

findings.title: No instrument measures GPU time, power, or the actual iPad
findings.observation: Every number in the perf plan is a count of draws or allocations, or an fps reading. Nothing measures what heats a laptop (GPU power and active residency), and nothing reads an actual iPad. ipad-probe drives macOS WebKit, and its own header says a clean run does not clear the iPad. DebugOverlay and Show Stats open by key, which a touch-only iPad does not have. In this state, every iPad claim, including the shadow-reset fix, is unproven.

(1) A power A/B script: the production build in local Chrome on a fixed scenario, with powermetrics running gpu_power, cpu_power and thermal samplers for 120 samples at 1 s, parsed into mean GPU mW and thermal pressure. This becomes the acceptance number for 'runs cool'. It needs sudo, so Kevin runs it or a sudoers rule scoped to powermetrics is added. (2) Per-pass timer queries in gpu-cost-probe. findings.title: WebKit feature gaps: most suspects ruled out in source; one binary check is left for the device
findings.observation: Ruled out in source: no FloatType texture is sampled with LinearFilter, so the OES_texture_float_linear gap is never hit (N8AO's R32F target uses NearestFilter, and src has no float textures). three's shaders get its highp prefix, and the terrain declares highp sampler2DArray, so mediump does not apply to three-built shaders. The composer's MSAA is 0, so there is no MSAA-resolve path. Tone mapping runs in the composer's NEUTRAL pass the same way in WebKit. Still open: the composer's RGBA16F buffers and N8AO's mixed R32F + RGBA16F multiple-render-target must be color-renderable on iPadOS. If they are not, the framebuffer is incomplete and the frame is black or garbage. Separately, TitleDiorama has no composer and so uses R3F's ACESFilmic default while the game uses NEUTRAL, which shifts colour between title and play on every platform.

findings.title: Spatial audio writes automation events and casts occlusion rays every frame
findings.observation: Every frame, SpatialAudioController calls setTargetAtTime on the master filter and on the reverb wet gain, even above ground where the target never changes. It also allocates a new filtered array of active sounds. For each active spatial sound it casts a recursive voxel occlusion ray and adds two more automation events. All of this runs at the frame rate. Each setTargetAtTime adds an event to the AudioParam timeline on the audio thread. The AudioContext is not suspended when the tab is hidden.

findings.proposal: Write automation only when the target changes by more than 1% (cache the last value). Run occlusion at 15 Hz round-robin, and skip the loop when no spatial sound is active. Suspend the AudioContext on visibilitychange to hidden and resume it on visible. Proving instrument: wrap AudioParam.prototype.setTargetAtTime and count calls per second during idle play, with a target of about 0.

findings.title: Per-frame CPU: 59 useFrame call sites plus one per mob, with allocations and repeated store writes
findings.observation: Outside tests there are 59 useFrame call sites in 45 files. About 54 mount on the game canvas, plus one per live mob (MobModel), XP orb and projectile: about 100 callbacks per frame on a 40-mob night. The Player loop allocates new Vector3s and objects every frame (lines 1077-1079 while airborne, 1191, 1224; 1039-1041 every 150 ms) and builds a filterPredicate closure. It writes fresh objects into the store every 150 ms through setAbilityCooldowns and setTargetEntity, even when nothing changed. MinimapSync rebuilds two entity arrays every 250 ms. The grass driver builds 8 arrays per frame. Each is small, but on the iPad's smaller heap the combined garbage-collection churn shows up as frame spikes, which push the governor down.

findings.proposal: Use module-level scratch vectors in the controller. Guard store writes with an equality check: setTargetEntity only when the id or health changes, setAbilityCooldowns only when a field changes. Merge the cheap uniform drivers (Terrain, FarField, Grass and Ocean all read mood and sun) into one ordered render-systems useFrame. Run mob animation as one system over mobsQuery instead of N React-owned callbacks. Proving instruments: Long Animation Frames (PerformanceObserver 'long-animation-frame') and JS self-time per frame in a production trace of the siege scenario, plus heap-sampling allocation rate before and after; on WebKit, the JS allocations timeline.
